correctness.rationale: In the even-parity five-cube model, a translated nonempty odd independent class contains zero and weight-two words corresponding to a pairwise-intersecting edge family F on five positions. The five weight-four test vertices require all degrees in F even; therefore F is empty or a full triangle. These give exactly singleton classes and 40 four-vertex two-coordinate cylinders. Disjoint cylinders are classified by their shared fixed coordinate and opposing prescribed bit. Counting unordered disjoint families gives \(A_q=1,40,300,360,70\) for \(q=0,1,2,3,4\), hence \(P_C(z)=70z^4+360z^7+300z^{10}+40z^{13}+z^{16}\). The q=4 supports use either one or two coordinate pairs, in 10 and 60 cases. The two standalone programs independently return every coefficient; the proof, not just the programs, certifies exhaustiveness.

value.rationale: The sixteen-vertex Clebsch graph is a canonical triangle-free strongly regular graph and a natural small test for strong odd coloring introduced in 2024. The classification of every odd independent color class by affine two-coordinate cylinders is a nontrivial structural obstruction, not a substitution into a general inequality. The complete nonconsecutive color-count spectrum and exact 10+60 classification distinguish 70 strong-odd optimum partitions from 1190 ordinary proper four-color partitions. These exact natural invariants are mathematically informative beyond a scalar chromatic number.
